definition_title: Generalized Reed–Muller evaluations and the rank test
natural_language_statement:
For any finite field $F$ with $q$ elements, let $\operatorname{RM}_q(d,R)$ be the $F$-linear span of the evaluations on all points of $F^d$ of monomials $z^a$ with $0\le a_j<q$ and $\sum_ja_j\le R$. Thus both the total-degree bound and each reduced individual-degree bound are imposed. Set
$$R=\left\lfloor\frac{(d-3)(q-1)-1}{2}\right\rfloor,\qquad \mathcal M(y)=V\operatorname{diag}(y)V^{\mathsf T},\qquad D(y)=\mathbf1\!\left[\operatorname{rank}_F\mathcal M(y)\le(1/2-\varepsilon/2)m\right].$$
Here $V$ has one row for every reduced monomial of degree at most $R$, evaluated using the public row order; $y$ is binary and its entries are embedded as zero and one in $F$. The transpose is the ordinary transpose. The code, the evaluation matrix and its rank are computed from this data rather than specified through desired properties.

These definitions fix the concrete deterministic test, which accepts noisy codewords without attempting to decode a message.

**Formalization Note** The auxiliary degree uses integer floor division; converting a negative degree to a natural number returns zero only on parameter values outside every construction assertion. Construction dimensions are much larger than three. The generalized code is not the binary Boolean-cube code. The rank test receives the ordered word and size, with no sampler seed or transcript.
definition:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_ExpandingCodes_PolynomialStretch_Sampler
set_option autoImplicit false
open scoped Classical

namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open scoped BigOperators
abbrev Monomials (F : Type*) [Fintype F] (d R : ℕ) :=
  {a : Fin d → Fin (Fintype.card F) // ∑ i, (a i).val ≤ R}
noncomputable def monomialEval {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {d R : ℕ}
    (a : Monomials F d R) (z : Fin d → F) : F := ∏ i, z i ^ (a.val i).val
noncomputable def reedMuller (F : Type*) [Field F] [Fintype F] (d R : ℕ) :
    Submodule F ((Fin d → F) → F) :=
  Submodule.span F (Set.range (monomialEval (F := F) (d := d) (R := R)))
/-- Integer floor before conversion; construction parameters make the numerator positive. -/
def auxiliaryDegree (q d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((((d : ℤ) - 3) * ((q : ℤ) - 1) - 1) / 2).toNat
noncomputable def evaluationMatrix {d n : ℕ} (g : Geometry d n) :
    Matrix (Monomials g.F d (auxiliaryDegree (Fintype.card g.F) d))
      (Fin (rowCount d n)) g.F :=
  fun a z => monomialEval a (g.rowOrder z)
noncomputable def testMatrix {d n : ℕ} (g : Geometry d n) (y : Word (rowCount d n)) :=
  (evaluationMatrix g * Matrix.diagonal (fun z => if y z = 0 then (0 : g.F) else 1)) *
    (evaluationMatrix g).transpose
noncomputable def rankTest (ε : ℝ) {d n : ℕ} (g : Geometry d n)
    (y : Word (rowCount d n)) : Bool := by
  classical
  exact decide ((testMatrix g y).rank ≤ (1 / 2 - ε / 2) * (rowCount d n : ℝ))

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
source: Isaac M Hair, Amit Sahai, Expanding Codes with Polynomial Stretch, STOC 2027 submission #824 (October 2026), printed p. 9 / PDF p. 10, §2.2, equation (5) and the definitions of V, ℳ and D.
